test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following methods does NOT consider historical cost of inventory?
solution:
The correct answer is** Retail price method.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Retail Price Method:**

 
 
• The retail price method estimates the ending inventory value based on the current retail prices, rather than the historical cost.
 
• This method uses the relationship between the cost and the retail price to value inventory, which can be particularly useful in retail businesses with large inventories.
 
• Since it does not rely on historical costs, it is not affected by changes in purchase prices over time, making it the correct answer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIFO (First-In, First-Out):**

 
 
• This method assumes that the oldest inventory items are sold first, and thus, the cost of goods sold is based on the historical cost of the oldest inventory.
 
• It ensures that the inventory on hand is valued at the most recent costs.
 
 
 
• **LIFO (Last-In, First-Out):**
 
 
• Under LIFO, the most recently purchased or produced items are considered sold first, making the cost of goods sold based on the historical cost of the latest inventory.
 
• This method can result in lower net income during inflationary periods as it matches current costs with current revenues.
 
 
 
• **Weighted Average:**
 
 
• The weighted average method calculates the cost of goods sold and ending inventory based on the average cost of all units available for sale during the period.
 
• This average cost takes into account the historical cost of all inventory items.
